relevance_reason: Only the abstract was available. It is a consensus reclassification of inherited epidermolysis bullosa and related skin fragility disorders. It does not mention the nephropathy-and-deafness subtype or its gene, so it gives only general naming context.

findings.statement: In a consensus expert review, Has et al. (2020) reclassified inherited epidermolysis bullosa (EB) using new clinical and molecular data. They introduced the concept of genetic disorders with skin fragility, with classical EB as the prototype. Disorders in which blisters are a minor feature, such as peeling skin, erosive, hyperkeratotic and connective tissue disorders with skin fragility, were placed in separate categories.
quotes: We sought to reclassify disorders with skin fragility, with a focus on EB, based on new clinical and molecular data.
we introduce the concept of genetic disorders with skin fragility, of which classical EB represents the prototype.
These include peeling skin disorders, erosive disorders, hyperkeratotic disorders, and connective tissue disorders with skin fragility.

relevance_reason: The paper describes the patients who define EBS7 (nephropathy, pretibial EB, deafness) and identifies a homozygous CD151 frameshift variant in them.

findings.statement: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin, 2 of them sibs, who had end-stage kidney disease. Along with hereditary nephritis, the sibs had sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor.
quotes: We examined CD151 in 3 MER2-negative patients (2 are sibs) of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease.
In addition to hereditary nephritis the sibs have sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor.

findings.statement: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) found that all 3 MER2-negative Indian Jewish patients with end-stage kidney disease were homozygous for a single-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140, and the authors predicted that the truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.
quotes: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
The resultant truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.

findings.statement: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) concluded that CD151 is essential for correct assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney and has functional significance in the skin. They suggested that it is probably a component of the inner ear and could play a role in erythropoiesis. They also reported that CD151 forms stable laminin-binding complexes with integrins.
quotes: We conclude that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membrane in kidney, has functional significance in the skin, is probably a component of the inner ear, and could play a role in erythropoiesis.
Tetraspanin CD151 forms very stable laminin-binding complexes with integrins alpha3beta1 and alpha6beta1 in kidney and alpha3beta1 and alpha6beta4 in skin.

findings.statement: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151 carries the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes; the patients were MER2-negative.
quotes: We show that CD151 expresses the MER2 blood group antigen and is located on erythrocytes.

relevance_reason: Title describes two siblings with hereditary nephritis, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and end-stage renal disease, which is the defining phenotype of this entry.

findings.statement: Kagan et al. (1988) reported 2 sibs with hereditary nephritis, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and end-stage renal disease; both sibs also had beta-thalassemia minor.
quotes: Occurrence of hereditary nephritis, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and beta-thalassemia minor in two siblings with end-stage renal disease.
